It is far too slow: one scene run takes about 3.5 seconds, 1A's 22 runs took 46 seconds of wall time, and a test walking 1A to 2B took 172 seconds. The owner wants the per-change gate and its tests to be fast. We need to know exactly where the time goes before deciding what to change.

YOUR TASK.
1. Write /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/factory-carry-matrix/profile-rollout/profile.py that measures, on the real story (`data/stories/continuity-initiative`, `load_story_package`, then `_legacy_package` from `storygame.personas`):
   a. Time to load the package, to run `_legacy_package`, to `RuntimeState.bootstrap`, to build a `RuntimeEngine`, to take `state.snapshot()`, and to `restore_snapshot()` (median of 20 where repeatable).
   b. One `default` 1A rollout through the draft's own rollout code: total time, turn count, and per-turn time.
   c. The same rollout under `cProfile`: save the stats to /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/factory-carry-matrix/profile-rollout/rollout.prof and the top 40 functions by cumulative time and the top 40 by total (self) time to /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/factory-carry-matrix/profile-rollout/profile.txt.
   d. A breakdown of each turn's time into the engine's phases: candidate projection (`engine.projector.project` as called by the rollout loop), `engine._activate_pacing`, and `engine.turn`; and inside `engine.turn`, the largest sub-steps you can attribute from the profile (validation, commit, world-model application, item facts, delivery text, prompt or payload building, pydantic validation or copying, deep copies). Name each with file:line.
   e. Whether the draft's process pool helps: how it starts workers (fork or spawn), what each worker loads at start, and the wall time for 1A's 22 runs with the pool versus run one after another in one process. Explain the 46 seconds for 22 runs.
   f. Repeated work across runs: how much of a scene run repeats an identical earlier run (for example every one-choice path replaying the same default turns of later scenes), and how many of 1A's runs share an identical prefix of turns before they diverge.
2. Run it; keep stdout in /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/factory-carry-matrix/profile-rollout/run.out.
3. Write /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/factory-carry-matrix/profile-rollout/report.md with sections: ## Fixed costs (table from 1a); ## One rollout (1b and 1d: per phase, ms per turn and share of the turn, file:line); ## Hot spots (the top functions from profile.txt that matter, what each does, and whether an offline scripted run needs it at all: the narrator prompt, payloads for a model and similar output are never read offline); ## Pool (1e); ## Repeated work (1f); ## Speedups (a ranked list; for each: what to change, in which file, whether it is factory code or engine code, the measured or estimated saving with how you estimated it, and the risk to the gate's correctness. Include at least: skipping work an offline run never reads, sharing turn prefixes or memoizing identical runs, pool start-up, and whether the gate's unit tests should run on a small fixture story instead of the real one (look at `tests/fixtures/story_source/` and `tests/story_source/helpers.py`). Mark measured numbers separately from estimates.

HARD RULES. Do not edit /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge or /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/factory-carry-matrix/attempt3. Do not round away measurements; report ms. Keep the whole probe under 20 minutes of run time.
